items.impact: Different generators may include or exclude plan-only IDs from requirements and total_requirements, changing coverage rates and orphan semantics for the same inputs.
items.statement: requirements permits IDs discovered only through plan-node references, orphaned_node_requirement_refs names those same absent-from-REQUIREMENTS IDs as orphans, while total_requirements counts only IDs in REQUIREMENTS.md; membership and counting treatment is therefore ambiguous.
items.title: Plan-only requirement IDs have conflicting semantics

items.title: Acceptance mappings lack referential validity

segments.summary: Reviewed all 196 core lines and all 17 assigned semantic and structural source units under exact and adversarial lenses. The schema provides a strict report shape and clear prose classifications, but leaves major semantic invariants, input snapshot identity, partial-failure states, cross-source reference validity, and dashboard truth unenforced.

cross_document_questions: Which document is authoritative when REQUIREMENTS.md, plan_graph/index.json, and acceptance_manifest.json disagree or change during generation?
Are plan-only requirement IDs included in requirements and total_requirements, or only recorded as orphaned_node_requirement_refs?
What contract proves that an acceptance_check_id exists, is active, is executable, and semantically covers the referenced requirement?
What consumer is allowed to treat the report as a blocking governance oracle, and how must it surface stale, partial, or failed generation?
research_queries: JSON Schema 2020-12 patterns for enforcing dependent array cardinality and discriminated states
content-addressed provenance patterns for multi-source generated governance reports
referential-integrity validation patterns for JSON artifacts spanning requirement and acceptance manifests
dashboard UX patterns for stale partial and internally inconsistent compliance data
